headline: Harvard study: Largest U.S. data centers emit more carbon than all of Denmark
claim: The roughly 400 largest U.S. data centers emitted more CO2 in a year than Denmark, according to a Harvard-led study.
notes: published 2026-11-16 (page date read via WebFetch). AP story carried by Spectrum News. Study in Nature Sustainability covers 403 large US data centers, May 2024 to April 2025; emissions are modeled estimates because operators do not disclose data, not direct measurements. Article also quotes an advocacy group (Climate Action Against Disinformation) and a heat-recovery company (Danfoss) on unrelated figures.

headline: Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
claim: Off-grid gas plants being built for data centers could emit about 345 million metric tons of CO2-equivalent per year if all announced plants are built.
notes: published 2026-11-24 (page date read via WebFetch). Projection, not a measurement: the 345 Mt/yr figure (BloombergNEF estimate, as cited) assumes every announced on-site plant is built; about 4.9 GW is operating today. Article reports over 100 announced US plants.
